winner.title: Draniki

evidence.authenticity: Traditional potato-onion draniki with the classic mushroom filling sandwiched between potato layers; explains the name (Belarusian word 'to tear'), per-capita potato consumption, breakfast origins, and traditional serving (sour cream, machanka, kvass). Author is not Belarusian.
evidence.precision: Potatoes by weight (700 g / about 4 medium); dried vs fresh mushroom weights; doneness cues: oil ready when a drop of mixture sizzles, about 4 min per side until golden, mixture should resemble apple sauce, spoon off starchy liquid. Pan size is only 'large frying pan'; no temperatures.
evidence.testing: No test kitchen, but gives tips: flip sparingly, food processor gives worse texture, how to manage starchy liquid, vegan egg swaps.
evidence.photos: Three uncaptioned step photos plus finished dish (seen via WebFetch); not clear they match key stages.
evidence.efficiency: Mushroom filling prepared while nothing waits; 20 min prep and 10-20 min cook is realistic, though 'difficult' rating is odd.
evidence.access: Everything at a US grocery; dried wild mushrooms are optional with fresh mushrooms given.

winner.why: Most traditional version with the best history context and gram weights plus clear doneness cues, edging out the chicken-stuffed Splendid Table version.

runnerUp.title: Draniki
runnerUp.source: The Splendid Table (Chef David Nayfeld, via The Inherited Plate)

evidence.authenticity: Belarusian-style potato pancake stuffed with chicken (meat-stuffed variant); chef author, Jewish-roots interview linked; Russian sour cream suggested.
evidence.precision: 2 lb Yukon Gold (4-5 large), 1/3 cup batter per pancake, 1/2 inch thick, 1/4 inch oil, 400F oven; cues: shimmering oil, fluffy dark golden about 4 min, add flour tbsp at a time if water pools. No pan size.
evidence.testing: Explains that salt draws out liquid while batter rests so keep adding flour; tasting a cooked bite of filling.
evidence.efficiency: Fry plus oven finish; reasonable, no stated total time.
evidence.access: Standard ingredients; meat grinder optional with food-processor alternative.

runnerUp.why: Very precise and well reasoned, but a stuffed-with-chicken variant with only a hero photo.

candidates.disqualified: Recipe is paywalled; no ingredients or steps visible

notes: Sites search found nothing. Best option from Darya Zorka (Belarusian author) is paywalled, so unusable. Nomad Paradise gives a simple flour-and-egg version with weights (700 g) and a lid step. Plain potato-only versions are less well documented than the mushroom-stuffed ones; the Belarus tourism page says the traditional recipe is just potato, onion, oil and salt.
